name: filos
description: Socratic PR review: understand the change, then review it.

enumDescriptions: Claude Code: the claude CLI, with its own login (subscription, API key, Bedrock or Vertex).
Codex: the OpenAI codex CLI, with its own login (ChatGPT account or API key).
filos.provider.markdownDescription: Agent CLI that runs every agent step: the comprehension graph, questions, grading, drafting and threads. Use **Filos: Choose Agent CLI…** to see which CLIs are installed and logged in. Read from user settings only, so a repository can't choose which program Filos runs.

filos.claude.path.description: Path to the claude CLI (Claude Code): a name on PATH, an absolute path, or ~/…. Read from user settings only, so a repository can't choose which program Filos runs.

filos.claude.model.description: Claude Code model alias passed to --model. Empty uses the CLI's default model, which may be slower and more expensive. Read from user settings only.

filos.claude.maxBudgetUsd.description: Spending cap in US dollars per Claude Code call (the comprehension pass, and each question, grading, drafting or thread step). Claude Code only: Codex reports no dollar cost, so filos.agentTimeoutSeconds is what bounds it. Read from user settings only, so a repository can't raise it.

filos.codex.path.description:
Path to the codex CLI (Codex): a name on PATH, an absolute path, or ~/…. An npm install's launcher (codex.js, or codex.cmd on Windows) is followed to the codex executable it starts; if Filos can't find it on Windows, set this to that codex.exe (under %APPDATA%
pm
ode_modules\@openai\codex
ode_modules\@openai\codex-win32-x64\vendor\x86_64-pc-windows-msvc in). Read from user settings only, so a repository can't choose which program Filos runs.

filos.codex.model.description: Codex model passed to --model. Empty uses Codex's default model. With a ChatGPT account Codex can't use every model (an API-only model fails with "not supported when using Codex with a ChatGPT account"). Read from user settings only.

filos.codex.useUserConfig.description: Load ~/.codex/config.toml (needed for a custom model provider such as company SSO). Filos's read-only lockdown still applies. Off (the default): Filos ignores that file, so its model and other settings don't apply; Codex still uses your login. Read from user settings only.

filos.agentTimeoutSeconds.description: Kill the agent CLI (Claude Code or Codex) after this many seconds (at most 3600). Read from user settings only.

filos.gh.path.description: Path to the GitHub CLI used to find the pull request and post reviews: a name on PATH, an absolute path, or ~/…. Filos uses gh's own login and never sees a token. Read from user settings only, so a repository can't choose which program Filos runs.

scripts.typecheck: tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.webview.json --noEmit && tsc -p harness/tsconfig.json --noEmit
scripts.package: npm run build && vsce package --no-dependencies --allow-missing-repository --skip-license -o dist/filos.vsix
scripts.test:e2e:vsix: npm run package && node dist/test/runE2E.js --vsix dist/filos.vsix

untrustedWorkspaces.description: The bundled sample works anywhere, and so does reviewing a pull request by its URL: its code goes into Filos's own storage. Reviewing the current branch, or listing the workspace repository's pull requests, runs git and gh in the folder, so it needs a trusted workspace.
